[RB-RAN-UPGRADE-REGRESSION#03] RAN software upgrade regression > Differential diagnosis: Versus the harmless upgrades Most upgrades produce nothing more than a brief dip in availability during the restart. A software change only becomes a suspect if quality is worse after the restart than before it, on the upgraded sites only. Versus a bad configuration push A configuration regression starts exactly at the change time without a restart, affects a router subtree or site group, and ends at a rollback record. An upgrade regression starts after the restart, tracks the software version, and may last days. ...
[RB-RAN-UPGRADE-REGRESSION#02] RAN software upgrade regression > Signature in the data: A software upgrade change on a site or group of sites, executed at night. A short availability dip during the restart is expected, typically one or two steps. Persistent quality loss after the restart. Elevated `drop_rate_pct`, lower `rrc_success_pct`, and sometimes a lower volume that does not recover on the following days. This is the difference from a config push, which is tied to a template and reverses at once. Version-specific. Only sites that received the new software are affected. ... Repeated restarts. .....
[RB-DNS-DEGRADATION#05] Core DNS degradation > Recommended actions: Ask core operations to check the DNS service: process health, resource usage, upstream resolvers and recent configuration. Fail over to a secondary resolver if one exists. Review query volume for abuse. Notify customer care that the problem is nationwide and short. Confirm recovery in `resolution_ms` and `query_success_pct` before closing.

# Nationwide Slow Data and Traffic Dip Incident Report

- **Classification:** incident
- **Root cause:** core_degradation at `CORE-DNS-01`
- **Confidence:** high (Direct evidence of software upgrade, core alarms, and KPI anomalies on CORE-DNS-01 closely preceding the onset, with maintenance, external events, and transport failures ruled out.)
- **Impact:** 2026-09-18 15:00 to 2026-09-18 16:38
- **Cause time:** 2026-09-18 13:59
- **Affected:** CORE-DNS-01, S-SAH-001, S-SAH-002, S-SAH-003, S-SAH-004

## Summary

Software patch upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 triggered a resolver service restart, leading to DNS timeouts and resolution latency spikes.

Nationwide slow data and traffic dip affecting query success percentage and resolution latency, starting at 15:00 and fully recovering by 16:38.

## Timeline

- 2026-09-18 13:59: Software patch 21.4.2 -> 21.4.3 applied on CORE-DNS-01 with a resolver service restart. [CHG-2026-0043]
- 2026-09-18 15:00: Earliest onset of slow data and traffic dip with query_success_pct dropping and resolution_ms rising. [T5, ANM-000238]
- 2026-09-18 15:08: Major DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE alarm raised on CORE-DNS-01. [ALM-000365]
- 2026-09-18 16:30: KPI metrics recovered for query_success_pct and resolution_ms. [T5]
- 2026-09-18 16:38: Major DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE alarm cleared on CORE-DNS-01. [ALM-000365]

## Evidence

- Detector alert active overlapping the incident window from 2026-09-18 10:00 to 2026-09-19 08:28. [T1, ALR-0021]
- A software upgrade change was executed on CORE-DNS-01 at 13:59 on 2026-09-18. [T3, CHG-2026-0043]
- A major DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE alarm was raised on CORE-DNS-01 at 15:08 and cleared at 16:38. [T2, ALM-000365]
- KPIs for CORE-DNS-01 showed query_success_pct dropping and resolution_ms spiking starting at 15:00. [T5, ANM-000238]
- No external events were reported across all regions during the window. [T7]

## Hypotheses

1. **core_degradation** at CORE-DNS-01: confirmed. The software upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 directly preceded the DNS timeout alarms and KPI degradation starting at 15:00. [CHG-2026-0043, ALM-000365, T5]

## Ruled out

- T4: No maintenance window was scheduled on CORE-DNS-01 and its parents during the incident window.
- T7: No external events were found for all regions between 2026-09-18 12:00 and 2026-09-18 18:00.

## Recommended actions

- Ask core operations to check the DNS service process health, resource usage, upstream resolvers, and recent configuration.
- Confirm recovery in resolution_ms and query_success_pct before closing.

confounders.why: Harmless software_upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 completed 54 min before the degradation; the DNS KPIs stayed normal until the onset and the same patch on other core nodes did nothing.

truth.notes: trap=change_on_root_node; CORE-DNS-01 degraded for about 99 min; nationwide latency up, volume down, RRC unaffected. Trap: a software upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 itself ran 54 min before the onset, so a hasty investigator blames the change. Settled by: (1) the DNS and RRC KPIs were normal for 54 min after the upgrade, while a configuration change takes effect at once; (2) the same patch under the same ticket went onto CORE-AMF-01 and CORE-UPF-01 at the same time and both stayed healthy; (3) the degradation ended by itself, with no rollback or other change at the recovery.
